title: Reported Speech Basics
grammar_goal: Boosts GRA by demonstrating the ability to indirectly report what others have said, which is highly useful in Speaking Part 2 and 3, and Task 2.

core_rule.formula: Subject + reporting verb (said, told, argued) + (that) + Subject + backshifted verb tense
core_rule.usage: When reporting what someone else said, shift the tense backwards (e.g., Present Simple -> Past Simple; 'will' -> 'would'; 'can' -> 'could'). Pronouns and time expressions may also need to change.

when_to_use: Task 2: Reporting the views of others (e.g., 'Some experts argue that climate change is...'). Note: Tense backshifting is sometimes optional for general truths.
Speaking Part 2: Telling a story and reporting a past conversation (e.g., 'My teacher told me that I needed to work harder.').
when_not_to_use: Do not backshift tenses if the reporting verb is in the present tense (e.g., 'He says that he is happy').
Do not use 'told' without an object (e.g., 'He told that...' is wrong. Use 'He said that...' or 'He told me that...').

ielts_examples.writing: Critics have argued that the new policy would negatively impact small businesses.
ielts_examples.speaking: My manager told me that I would be promoted the following month.

repair_section.wrong: She told that she will come to the party.
repair_section.correct: She said that she would come to the party.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: She mentioned that she intended to attend the gathering.

repair_section.wrong: He asked me where do I live.
repair_section.correct: He asked me where I lived.
repair_section.better_band_upgrade: He inquired about my place of residence.

vietnamese_learner_mistakes: Forgetting to change the word order in reported questions (e.g., 'He asked what time is it' instead of 'He asked what time it was').
Using 'said me' instead of 'told me' or 'said to me'.
Failing to shift pronouns and time words (e.g., keeping 'tomorrow' instead of 'the next day' when reporting past speech).

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: My friend said me he is tired.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: My friend told me he was tired.

mini_sentence_repair_exercise.wrong_sentence: The examiner asked me what is my name.
mini_sentence_repair_exercise.correct_sentence: The examiner asked me what my name was.

image_prompt_fallback: An illustration of two people talking with speech bubbles. One person's bubble has quotation marks (direct speech), and the other's has a thought bubble summarizing it (reported speech).

quiz.question: Choose the correct reported speech form of: 'I can help you tomorrow,' John said to Mary.

options.A: John said to Mary that he can help her tomorrow.
options.B: John told Mary that he could help her the next day.
options.C: John told Mary that I could help you tomorrow.
options.D: John said Mary that he could help her the next day.

quiz.explanation: Option B is correct. 'Said to' becomes 'told' (with an object). 'Can' backshifts to 'could'. Pronouns change appropriately, and 'tomorrow' changes to 'the next day'.
